newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE ends up bit as three-month CD yield slips.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE ends up bit as three-month CD yield slips.

text.p: The benchmark March three-month euroyen futures contract ended up slightly on Monday, buoyed slightly by weak Tokyo stocks and firm Japanese government bonds (JGBs), although the topside remained limited.

In the open market, around 40 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.57 percent, the lowest since May 21 this year, on a sense that interest rates may dip over the coming months, traders said.

Little impact was detected from weak Tokyo stocks, although the euroyen market did gain some peripheral support, traders said, noting that euroyen futures had become somewhat unresponsive to Nikkei moves recently.
The BOJ conducted a neutral money market operation this morning by injecting 200 billion yen.
By afternoon, overnight call money was being traded at around 0.48 percent, and traders said this was likely to become the weighted average.
